claim: As of 2022, 91.1% of YouTube channels had fewer than 1,000 subscribers, with only 10.1 million channels (8.86%) clearing the subscriber half of the Partner Program's ad-revenue threshold.
stance_target: The position that the overwhelming majority of people who start a channel never reach even the eligibility gate for platform income
scope_conditions: 2022 data, global, all YouTube channels including inactive and abandoned ones; the post is a secondary aggregation crediting a single external source (timqueen.com/youtube-number-of-channels) with no method, sampling frame or confidence interval disclosed; no country disaggregation
quoted_support: 91.1% of YouTube Channels have under 1k Subscribers... In 2022 10.1 million YouTube channels have at least 1,000 subscribers... The exact percentage of YouTube channels with over 1,000 subscribers is 8.86%.

claim: Channels above 100,000 subscribers numbered 321,100 in 2022 (0.28% of all channels, about 1 in 350) and channels above one million numbered 32,300 (0.028%, about 1 in 3,600), giving an order-of-magnitude drop per subscriber decade.
stance_target: The position that the creator audience distribution is a steep power law in which career-viable audience sizes are reached by a fraction of a percent of participants
scope_conditions: 2022 secondary aggregation crediting timqueen.com; global; no method disclosed; counts include channels of media companies and music labels, not only individual creators
quoted_support: There are 321,100 YouTube channels with at least 100,000 subscribers. Which is 0.28% of all YouTube channels or around 1 in 350... Less than 33K YouTube channels have more than 1 million subscribers. 32,300. That is 0.028 percent of all YouTube channels or about 1 in 3,600 channels.
